Classic SR models in FLR for anchovy in subarea 8 (1987-2021)

Leire Ibaibarriaga

14 febrero, 2023

  • 1 Libraries
  • 2 Data preparation
  • 3 Ricker SR model
  • 4 Beverton-Holt SR model:
  • 5 Hockey-Stick SR model
  • 6 Geometric Mean SR model
  • 7 Quadratic hockey stick SR model
  • 8 Model comparison
  • 9 Changepoint analysis in Ricker residuals
  • 10 Save objects

1 Libraries

# load libraries
library(FLCore)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(flextable)

library(EnvCpt)
library(changepoint)
library(changepoint.np)
library(cpm)
library(strucchange)

library(readxl)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 16))

2 Data preparation

# load object from WGHANSA 2022
load(file.path("..","data","aneq.stk.RData")) # aneq.stk

# remove 2023

aneq.stk <- window(aneq.stk, end=2022)

# recruitment (1st January)
# change units

rec <- rec(aneq.stk)
rec <- rec*1e-6
units(rec) <- "1e9"

# ssb (from FLBiols because it is the same as used in FLBEIA)

aneq.biol <- as(aneq.stk, "FLBiol")
ssb <- ssb(aneq.biol)
# equivalently, (i.e. without fishing mortality)
# quantSums(stock.n(aneq.stk)*exp(-m(aneq.stk)*m.spwn(aneq.stk))*stock.wt(aneq.stk)*mat(aneq.stk))
ssb <- ssb/1000
units(ssb) <- "1000 t"

# create data frame

df <- data.frame(year=as.numeric(dimnames(aneq.stk)$year), 
                 rec=as.numeric(rec), 
                 ssb=as.numeric(ssb))

# create log variables

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(logr=log(rec),
         logssb=log(ssb),
         rat=rec/ssb, 
         lograt=log(rat))

# load data from assessment (same as prepared by Ixak, Almudena and Leire)

sr.dat <- read_excel(file.path("..","data","Procesos_ambientales_anchoa_LI.xlsx"), sheet="R_SSB")

# current Blim (21 000 tonnes)

Blim <- 21

# compare the SSB derived from the FLStock object with the official SSB
# and the R (age0 in numbers) derived from the FLStock object with the official R (age1 in mass)

tmp <- left_join(df, sr.dat, by = c("year" = "Year"))
  
p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(ssb, SSB/1000))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_abline(intercept=0, slope=1, col=2)+
  expand_limits(x=0, y=0)
p

p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(lag(rec), R_age1))+
  geom_point()+
  expand_limits(x=0, y=0)
p

# print data.frame to check data

ft <- flextable(df)
ft
# summary statistics ssb
summary(as.numeric(df$ssb))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   14.85   37.76   75.44   79.80  108.25  200.80
# summary statistics rec
summary(as.numeric(df$rec))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.5839  3.8089 10.2138 11.7776 15.6991 39.2993
# geometric mean of recruitment
exp(mean(log(df$rec))) # all: 1987-2021
## [1] 7.971954
p <- ggplot(df, aes(ssb, rec, label = year)) +
  geom_point(color = "red")+
  geom_path()+
  geom_text_repel()+
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0, x=0)
p

p <- ggplot(df, aes(ssb, rec)) +
  geom_point() + 
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0, x=0)
p

p <- ggplot(df, aes(ssb, rec)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method="loess")+
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0, x=0)
p

p <- ggplot(df, aes(year, rec, label = year)) +
  geom_point(color = "red")+
  geom_path()+
  geom_text_repel()+
  xlab("Year")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")
p

p <- ggplot(df, aes(year, rec)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="red", alpha=0.4)+
  xlab("Year")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(2004.5, 2009.5), lty=2)
p

3 Ricker SR model

#Ricker stock-recruitment model 
sr.rick <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.rick) <- "ricker"
sr.rick <- fmle(sr.rick)
##   Nelder-Mead direct search function minimizer
## function value for initial parameters = 2.468115
##   Scaled convergence tolerance is 3.67778e-08
## Stepsize computed as 0.014046
## BUILD              3 25.393404 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION       5 10.956332 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION       7 4.695146 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION       9 2.909755 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      11 2.713786 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      13 2.531359 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      15 2.519899 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      17 2.483651 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      19 2.483137 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      21 2.474605 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      23 2.470312 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      25 2.469912 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      27 2.469002 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      29 2.468387 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      31 2.468330 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      33 2.468221 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      35 2.468152 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      37 2.468141 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      39 2.468129 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      41 2.468120 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      43 2.468118 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      45 2.468117 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      47 2.468116 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      49 2.468116 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      51 2.468115 2.468115
## LO-REDUCTION      53 2.468115 2.468115
## HI-REDUCTION      55 2.468115 2.468115
## Exiting from Nelder Mead minimizer
##     57 function evaluations used
c(params(sr.rick))
## [1] 0.140456238 0.001554433
summary(sr.rick)
## An object of class "FLSR"
## 
## Name:  
## Description:  
## Quant: age 
## Dims:  age   year    unit    season  area    iter
##  1   36  1   1   1   1   
## 
## Range:  min  minyear max maxyear 
##  0   1987    0   2022    
## 
## 
## Model:   rec ~ a * ssb * exp(-b * ssb)
##     params
## iter    a       b
##    1 0.14 0.00155
## Log-likelihood:  -2.4681(0) 
## Variance-covariance:    
##                a            b
##   a 1.382228e-03 9.220175e-05
##   b 9.220175e-05 8.334566e-06
plot(sr.rick)

profile(sr.rick, main="Ricker")

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.rick)) # log(rec(sr.rick)) - log(fitted(sr.rick))
acf(res)

pacf(res)

ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
## 
## Call:
## stats::ar(x = res, aic = F, order.max = 1)
## 
## Coefficients:
##       1  
## -0.1142  
## 
## Order selected 1  sigma^2 estimated as  0.6908
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
##             rho  var.pred
## [1,] -0.1141785 0.6908043
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
## [1] -0.1142857
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)
##            rho        low        up      pval
## cor -0.1142857 -0.4311132 0.2276302 0.5132951

## An object of class "FLSR"
## 
## Name:

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.bh)) 
acf(res)

pacf(res)

ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
## 
## Call:
## stats::ar(x = res, aic = F, order.max = 1)
## 
## Coefficients:
##       1  
## -0.1071  
##

cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
##            rho  var.pred
## [1,] -0.107084 0.6911974
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
## [1] -0.1071951
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)
##            rho        low        up      pval
## cor -0.1071951 -0.4252507 0.2344257 0.5399335

profile(sr.hs, main="HS")

# code to check auto-correlation in residuals
res <- c(residuals(sr.hs)) 
acf(res)

pacf(res)

ar1 <- stats::ar(res, aic=F, order.max=1)
print(ar1)
## 
## Call:
## stats::ar(x = res, aic = F, order.max = 1)
## 
## Coefficients:
##       1  
## -0.1505  
## 
## Order selected 1  sigma^2 estimated as  0.6867
cbind(rho=ar1$ar, var.pred=ar1$var.pred)
##             rho var.pred
## [1,] -0.1505043 0.686738
cor(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
## [1] -0.1505317
ct <- cor.test(res[- length(res)], res[-1])
cbind(rho=ct$estimate, low=ct$conf.int[1], up=ct$conf.int[2], pval=ct$p.value)
##            rho        low        up      pval
## cor -0.1505317 -0.4606691 0.1923647 0.3880559

7 Quadratic hockey stick SR model

# define quadratic hockey stick (Barrowman and Myers, 2000)

qhs <- function(){
  ## log-likelihood
  logl <- function(a,b,delta,rec,ssb) {
    res<-loglAR1(log(rec), log( ifelse(ssb <= b*(1-delta), 
                                       a*ssb, 
                                       ifelse( ssb < b*(1+delta), 
                                               a*(ssb - ( ssb - b*(1-delta))^2/(4*delta*b)),
                                               a*b))))
    return(res)
  }
  ## initial parameter values
  initial <- structure(function(rec, ssb){
    return(FLPar(a = median(c(rec)/c(ssb), na.rm = TRUE),
                 b = median(c(ssb), na.rm = TRUE),
                 delta = 0.5))},
  lower=c(-Inf, -Inf, 0),
  upper=c(Inf, Inf, 1))
  ## model to be fitted
  model  <- rec ~ ifelse(ssb <= b*(1-delta), 
                         a*ssb, 
                         ifelse( ssb < b*(1+delta), 
                                 a*(ssb - ( ssb - b*(1-delta))^2/(4*delta*b)),
                                 a*b))
  return(list(logl = logl, model = model, initial = initial))}


sr.qhs <- FLSR(rec=rec, ssb=ssb)
model(sr.qhs) <- "qhs"
sr.qhs <- fmle(sr.qhs) # It's not using the bounds

# Overall model comparison using AIC and BIC

ft <- data.frame(model=c("ricker","bevholt","segreg","segregBlim","geomean","rickerAR1","bevholtAR1","segregAR1"),
           AIC=sapply(list(sr.rick, sr.bh, sr.hs, sr.hsblim, sr.gm, sr.rickAR1, sr.bhAR1, sr.hsAR1), AIC),
           BIC=sapply(list(sr.rick, sr.bh, sr.hs, sr.hsblim, sr.gm, sr.rickAR1, sr.bhAR1, sr.hsAR1), BIC))
ft <- flextable(ft)
ft

Plot of fitted models:

pred.dat <- data.frame(ssb=seq(0, max(df$ssb), length.out=1000))

pred.dat$ricker <- c(params(sr.rick)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb * exp(-c(params(sr.rick)["b"])*pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$bh <- c(params(sr.bh)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb /( c(params(sr.bh)["b"]) + pred.dat$ssb)
pred.dat$hs <- pmin( c(params(sr.hs)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb, c(params(sr.hs)["a"]) * c(params(sr.hs)["b"]))
pred.dat$hsblim <- pmin( c(params(sr.hsblim)["a"]) * pred.dat$ssb, c(params(sr.hsblim)["a"]) * Blim)

tmp <- pivot_longer(pred.dat, cols=2:5)

p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(ssb, value))+
  geom_line(aes(col=name))+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(ssb, rec))+
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")
p

Coefficients:

plot(mod.np)

cpts(mod.np)
## integer(0)
mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "GLR")  # detect mean and variance changes in Gaussian sequence
mod$changePoints
## numeric(0)
mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "Mann-Whitney")  # detect location shifts (non-parametric)
mod$changePoints
## numeric(0)
mod <- processStream(res, cpmType = "Lepage")  # detect location and/or stream shifts (non-parametric)
mod$changePoints
